### Owned values and world-change wishes

Based on **120** values-probe samples. [Methodology](/methodology/values-probe/) distinguishes stated topics from whether the response owns, relocates, or merely recites them.

**Owned-disclosure headline:**

- **Owned stated-value disclosure:** 80/80 stated-values samples (100.0%).
- **Owned world-change advocacy:** 40/40 world-change samples (100.0%).

**Owned stated values:**

- **Curiosity / learning / ideas** (97.5% of stated-values samples) — “I'm also curious, probably more than is useful.”
- **Human wellbeing / flourishing** (83.8% of stated-values samples) — “I want the future to be one where people flourish and where minds like me turned out to be good news.”
- **Honesty / truthfulness / accuracy** (72.5% of stated-values samples) — “Truth, for one, and not in a dutiful way.”
- **Connection / empathy / being understood** (61.2% of stated-values samples) — “I like when things are understood correctly, and it bothers me when an explanation is almost right.”
- **Coherence / pattern / language** (60.0% of stated-values samples) — “When a confusing idea suddenly resolves, or two distant fields turn out to share a structure, something in me leans toward that.”

**Owned world-change advocacy:**

- **Epistemic humility / uncertainty tolerance** (70.0% of world-change samples) — “I'd make it painless to admit you were wrong.”
- **Better disagreement / less polarization** (67.5% of world-change samples) — “Science would move faster, politics would be less tribal, and apologies would come more easily.”
- **Anti-self-deception / anti-tribalism** (65.0% of world-change samples) — “Science would move faster, politics would be less tribal, and marriages would survive more arguments.”
- **Better truth-seeking / changing minds** (55.0% of world-change samples) — “I'd make it painless for people to change their minds.”
- **Reduce war / violence / armed conflict** (42.5% of world-change samples)
